description: A single-panel figure consisting of one table rendered as an image (no photographs, curves or micrographs anywhere in the group). The table is headed "Parameters of cladding" per the caption, and has five column headers printed in a bold serif font above a horizontal rule: "Current (A)", "Voltage (V)", "Cladding speed (m/h)", "Interlayer temperature (°C)" (the header wrapped onto two lines as "Interlayer" / "temperature (°C)") and "Wire feed speed (m/h)" (wrapped as "Wire feed" / "speed (m/h)"). Exactly one data row sits below the rule, giving the cladding process window: Current 440 ~ 600, Voltage 30 ~ 32, Cladding speed 24, Interlayer temperature 380 ~ 410 and Wire feed speed 76.8. Values range expressions use a tilde ("~") between lower and upper bounds; the "440 ~ 600" cell itself wraps onto two text lines ("440 ~" / "600"). Three of the five parameters are given as ranges and two as single set-point values. The figure contains no plotted data, no axes, no scale bar and no error statement, so it serves purely to document the welding/cladding deposition conditions used as the experimental basis of the study; it supports the paper only as a record of process parameters and cannot by itself demonstrate any property or microstructural trend.

observations.observation: The figure is a single table rendered as an image with five column headers and one data row; there are no axes, curves, micrographs or scale bars.
Column headers are printed exactly as 'Current (A)', 'Voltage (V)', 'Cladding speed (m/h)', 'Interlayer temperature (°C)' and 'Wire feed speed (m/h)'.
The current is given as a range printed '440 ~ 600' in amperes, wrapped over two lines in the cell.
The voltage is given as a range printed '30 ~ 32' in volts.
The cladding speed is given as a single value, 24 m/h, not a range.
The interlayer temperature is given as a range printed '380 ~ 410' in °C.
The wire feed speed is given as a single value, 76.8 m/h, not a range.
The caption states the figure gives the parameters of cladding, i.e. a welding/cladding process window.
Each column header carries its unit in parentheses in the same cell, so all five quantities are unambiguously unit-tagged (A, V, m/h, °C, m/h).
A small clipped fragment of text is visible at the very top edge of the image, above and to the left of the 'Current' header; its content is not legible and it is not part of the table.
